newsitem.title: MEXICO: British mission to explore Mexico airports in July.
newsitem.headline: British mission to explore Mexico airports in July.

text.p: Some 50 British companies will send representatives to Mexico in July in search of opportunities to invest in airports, the British ambassador to Mexico said on Thursday.

"We are expecting a mission in July of 50 different companies specialising in airport privatisation...They will stay in Mexico for a period of two weeks exploring opportunities for investment," ambassador Adrian Beamish told a news conference here.

On a three-day visit to Mexico, the president of the Confederation of British Industry, Adair Turner, told the same news conference a number of British companies were watching the privatisation of Mexico's petrochemical sector closely, with a view to future investments in the sector.

"Yesterday, we had a meeting with the director of (Mexican oil company) Pemex and with the minister of energy, who made sure we were fully up to date with the progress of privatisation in the petrochemical sector," he added.
In 1996, the Mexican government decided to allow foreign investors to buy up to 49 percent of the country's petrochemical plants.
Turner said he would discuss the privatisation of Mexican airports at a meeting with the minister of communications and transport later on Thursday.
He added that the development of infrastructure in Mexico over the next decade would also be of great interest to British investors. ((--Cyntia Barrera Diaz, Mexico City newsroom +525 728 9549))
